reasons: Claimed status 'missing' is supported: Article XXI addresses only Licensee's return of Licensor materials, and no cited paragraph (Art. XX, confidentiality, general provisions) contains transition assistance, data export or deletion-timing terms, so there is no existing clause sitting at the preferred or fallback position that would make this over-flagging.

The redline is a clean insertion (new subsection (c)) that leaves the original paragraph untouched and tracks the model language closely: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. The legal-retention carve-out is a reasonable, non-prejudicial refinement.
The comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains what changed and why in two sentences, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.
Insertion is placed in the termination article as the redline guidance directs, and deterministic checks confirm the transition/data-return language is present.
